messages:
alice-support: Customer frank@west-amber reports a spike of 403s after yesterday's key rotation. Affected: mobile SDKs only (iOS/Android), web clients fine.
ben-oncall: got tenant id and sample request from Frank. stacktrace shows `invalid_apikey`. Any recent proxy or CDN changes? :thinking:
frank-customer: attaching log snippet from mobile app repro: `Authorization: Bearer xxxxx` then 403. Happens intermittently, ~30% of requests. Repro steps: login -> call /v1/generate -> 403.
charlie-devops: nothing changed in CDN config. Rotation job rotated vault path /secret/keys/west-amber and pushed new KMS-wrapped value to vault. Can you paste request headers (no secrets) and the server-side auth logs?
alice-support: paste from prod auth service (redacted):
```
[2026-01-29T14:12:02Z] tenant=west-amber request_id=abcd1234 api_key_id=rot-2026-01-29 result=403 reason=key_not_found
[2026-01-29T14:12:12Z] tenant=west-amber request_id=abcd1235 api_key_id=rot-2026-01-29 result=200
[2026-01-29T14:12:22Z] tenant=west-amber request_id=abcd1236 api_key_id=old-2025-12-01 result=403 reason=key_revoked
```
charlie-devops: interesting — we see the new key id (`rot-2026-01-29`) being seen by auth; some requests succeed, some hit `old-...` and get revoked. Sounds like a client-side cache of the old key is still being used by parts of the fleet.
daria-eng: mobile SDK caches API key from local storage and uses an exponential backoff refresh. If device hasn't fetched the new config, it keeps the old bearer until TTL. Could be the issue. Frank, do you rotate keys server-side only, or do you push an in-app config update?
frank-customer: we rotate centrally and rely on clients to fetch config on next app start. We didn't force-refresh. Most users updated their app, but some background processes keep old token.
eve-sre: also saw ~15% of requests coming via our auth-proxy pool labeled `ap-proxy-c-19` that still had long-lived connections to the upstream auth service from before rotation. If the proxy had a pinned connection and cached an upstream token, that could explain partial success.
harry-support-lead: two parallel causes likely: client local cache + connection-pinned auth-proxy. Let's run quick repro and mitigation steps: 1) rotate with short grace window and notify clients to fetch config; 2) flush long-lived connections on auth-proxy; 3) add additional logging to identify which IPs are sending old key ids.
ben-oncall: I can trigger a rolling restart for auth-proxy pool ap-proxy-c-*. Also adding a header on rotation to force clients to refresh: `x-config-version: 2026-01-29` — can we implement server-side response to reject old keys after a short grace?
daria-eng: temporary mitigation: extend grace to 5m and send push notification to mobile SDK to refresh config. Longer term: publish a revocation window + client-facing push API for immediate refresh.
vault-bot: rotation job rot-2026-01-29 completed: vault-path=/secret/keys/west-amber new-version=3 wrapped-by=kms-alias/alpha-kms. No errors during unwrap.
charlie-devops: note — some devices are still using an older KMS alias mapping (alpha-kms vs alpha-kms-v2) because our infra change renamed the alias in the last maintenance. If client-side unwrapping is attempted (edge case), alias mismatch would fail. But our config uses server-side unwrap so unlikely.
alice-support: Action items: (1) ben to restart auth-proxy pool now; (2) charlie to scan IPs and show which requests had old key id; (3) daria to push in-app config refresh via our push gateway; (4) support to notify customer and advise short-lived workaround (force-app-restart).
ben-oncall: restarting ap-proxy-c-19 -> DONE. Observing drop in 403s from 32% to ~8% in last 3 minutes.
charlie-devops: scan results: 84% of 403s came from three IP ranges belonging to older app versions (v1.3.0 and v1.3.1). I've opened an internal ticket to flag these tenants for forced refresh.
daria-eng: push refresh sent to approx 60% of active devices for west-amber. We'll follow up if spike persists.
frank-customer: thanks — mobile team will ship hotfix with forced fetch on next foreground event. Appreciate fast help.
harry-support-lead: follow-up: update runbook to add 'flush proxy connections' step as standard for host-side key rotations and include an explicit client-refresh push when rotating keys. Closing once no 403s for 30m. :thumbsup:
